title: Integral change of middle base in an oriented product
statement:
Let $f:X\to B$, $h:B'\to B$ and $v:T\to B'$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $h$ integral [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Put $X'=X\times_BB'$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projection $r:X'\to X$ and structure map $f':X'\to B'$. Form the oriented products of small etale topoi [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, lem-trf-oriented-product-universal]
$$E'=X'_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{B'_{\mathrm{Et}}}T_{\mathrm{Et}},\qquad E=X_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{B_{\mathrm{Et}}}T_{\mathrm{Et}},$$
where the right structure map for $E$ is $hv$. The canonical geometric morphism $c:E'\to E$ induced by $(r,h,1_T)$ and the structural oriented arrow is an equivalence of topoi: its inverse-image and direct-image functors are mutually quasi-inverse. This equivalence is compatible with projection to $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$ via $r$ and with projection to $T_{\mathrm{Et}}$. In particular postcomposition with $c$ induces an equivalence of the full categories of points, with their possibly noninvertible $2$-morphisms in the direct-image convention [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. No finite-presentation, finite-type, Noetherian, or finiteness assumption on $h$ is imposed.
